Skynet optimises a DSPy program: a signature, a module or workflow, and the instructions and demonstrations used by its language-model calls.
model_config selects the generation model and stores its temperature, token limit, provider, and billing source.
optimizer_kwargs contains one budget mode and the optional merge, minibatch, PxN, target-score, and cost-ceiling controls.

A reflective optimiser that improves instructions using trajectories, feedback, minibatches, and Pareto selection.

The feedback model that reads GEPA trajectories and written feedback and proposes revised instructions.

Skynet turns a task definition, examples, and a metric into a measured DSPy optimisation. GEPA searches the program's instructions and demonstrations, while Skynet handles validation, execution, cost controls, results, export, and serving.
Optimize
Workflow
Optimisation

The completed run records baseline and selected-program scores, split sizes, per-example results, logs, token use, model activity, timing, and cost. You can inspect or export the saved program, or run it through the serving API.
GEPA uses the dataset, metric, and feedback model to propose and evaluate changes to the program.
What each run produces
Skynet stores the submitted configuration, progress, logs, scores, model usage, example-level results, and a runnable DSPy program.
Initialisation
GEPA changes instructions and demonstrations inside the DSPy program. It does not fine-tune the selected models.

auto.features.tutorial.lib.steps.literal: Each dot is a prompt the optimiser tried, with its score. Lines link a prompt to the one it grew from. Drag Filter by generation to step through the search, and click a dot to see its full prompt and per-example scores.

Search runs by meaning, in English or Hebrew. Choose where to look: Mine, Shared with me, or Public. Press / to jump to the search box, and use Filters to narrow by model, module, optimiser, type or date.
auto.features.tutorial.lib.steps.templat: The Signature says what goes in and what comes out. The metric is a function that scores each answer from 0 to 1, and the optimiser tries to raise that score. By default an AI assistant drafts both for you, so check and edit them.

Name your run, then check the summary: data, models, optimiser and estimated cost. Use Edit to go back to any stage. When it looks right, click Submit optimisation below. We'll show you a sample finished run next.

At the top there is navigation to the dashboard, text labelling, submitting a new {p1}, and semantic search across existing runs. At the bottom, the run history appears grouped by date. Through the ⋯ next to a {p2} you can share, rename, clone, pin, or delete.
Try the optimised program here: type or dictate an input and watch the answer stream in.
Everything the optimiser logged, newest first. Use Quiet, Normal or Verbose to show more or less detail, filter the Level or Logger columns, and download the logs as CSV or Excel.
